resolution: Email35 adds the per-workspace send cap (#38) to Runtime and shows it in the App. Runtime32 caps the emails one workspace can send: two rolling windows, an hour and 24 hours, set from the helper's environment by EMAIL_RUNTIME_SEND_LIMIT_HOURLY and EMAIL_RUNTIME_SEND_LIMIT_DAILY, each a whole number from 1 to 10000. Any other value, the empty string included, stops the helper from starting. When a setting is absent the hosted form helper (form mode with registration_admission "host_authority") uses 200 an hour and 2,000 a day, and a self-hosted helper has no cap. A Send takes its slot, keyed by its Run id, in the same locked step that checks the cap just before the provider is called; the slot is given back only for a failure before the provider call or a definitive SMTP rejection, so accepted, partly accepted and uncertain Sends count and a retry never counts twice. Past a limit the Send is refused before any provider call: the Run ends failed with primary_outcome send_limit_reached and the kept draft carries EMAIL_SEND_LIMIT_REACHED. App13 shows it on the draft: "Not sent. This workspace has sent 200 emails in the last hour, its limit. Sending starts again at about 2:20 PM. This message is kept, and receiving email is not affected." Receiving, reading and organizing mail are not capped. The reviewed Send output schema is unchanged. No Host contract changes. Both Kit42 consumers retain the exact published Host134 bytes, producer metadata and corresponding source. The detached Email35 manifest must resolve final source and public artifacts; this template does not claim CI, publication or live deployment acceptance.

email.kit_compatibility: Host138 must be deployed before this App. Both consumers retain exact Host134 Kit alpha.42 with app-owned domain modules. Runtime32 preserves all fresh provider, OAuth, external-image, commit and disclosure guards and Send exact-message review; timing diagnostics never supply authority. App13 adds only the send-cap notice; Send authority is unchanged.

supported_environment.runtime_platform: POSIX with durable private storage and HTTPS

limitations: Operator-managed developer preview, not production Gmail/Outlook parity.
Latency acceptance requires measured current Host and Runtime callback, cached compose and sync-page results; a build alone does not establish those targets.
OAuth configuration, purpose-specific Host gates/keys, reviewed grants and durable Runtime custody are required.
Resource publication for Task/Knowledge integration needs separate reviewed finite or explicitly Host-issued until_revoked consent; technical renewal alone does not grant it.
